identity.title: 400 pc Imaging of a Massive Quasar Host Galaxy at a Redshift of 6.6

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report high spatial resolution ($\sim$0.076$''$, 410 pc) Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array imaging of the dust continuum and the ionized carbon line \[C II\] in a luminous quasar host galaxy at $z=6.6$

evidence.quote: The resulting NIR location of the quasar is 03$^\mathrm{h}$05$^\mathrm{m}$16$^\mathrm{s}\!$.919, –31$^\circ$50$^\prime$55.86$''$ with an uncertainty of 0.02$''$
resulting in $z_\mathrm{[CII]}=6.61391\pm0.00015$
The resulting NIR location of the quasar is 03$^\mathrm{h}$05$^\mathrm{m}$16$^\mathrm{s}\!$.919, –31$^\circ$50$^\prime$55.86$''$ with an uncertainty of 0.02$''$
resulting in $z_\mathrm{[CII]}=6.61391\pm0.00015$

distance_source.value: Gaussian fit to the [C II] line in these data

evidence.quote: The resulting NIR location of the quasar is 03$^\mathrm{h}$05$^\mathrm{m}$16$^\mathrm{s}\!$.919, –31$^\circ$50$^\prime$55.86$''$ with an uncertainty of 0.02$''$
resulting in $z_\mathrm{[CII]}=6.61391\pm0.00015$

question.value: What are the distribution and kinematics of [C II] gas and dust on ~400 pc scales in the z=6.6 quasar host J0305-3150, and what causes the observed cavities?

evidence.quote: The unprecedented high resolution of the observations reveals a complex morphology of gas within 3 kpc of the accreting central black hole.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01532.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: [C II] at 249.6 GHz in one 1.875 GHz band; three other 1.875 GHz bands for continuum at 252.1, 264.6, 266.6 GHz

evidence.quote: Three other bandpasses of 1.875 GHz each were placed to measure the FIR continuum at observed frequencies of 252.1, 264.6, and 266.6 GHz.
The ALMA observations covered the redshifted \[C II\] line observed at 249.6 GHz
in configuration C43-8
The number of antennas was 43 with baselines between 92 and 13,894 m.
The final beam using natural weighting has a size of 0.076$''$ $\times$ 0.071$''$, which corresponds to 410 pc $\times$ 385 pc at $z=6.6$.
The rms noise around the redshifted \[C II\] line is 87 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ per 30 MHz bin (36 km s$^{-1}$).
The total observing time was 7.6 hr, of which 3.5 hr were on-source.
we observed J0305–3150 between 2017 November 12 and 18 with ALMA in configuration C43-8.

evidence.quote: we recomputed the near-infrared (NIR) location of the quasar by correcting the positions of nearby stars with a match in the GAIA DR2 catalog
has a black hole mass of $\sim1\times10^9$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ (cite: ven13; der14; maz17b)

what.value: Dust SED shape: T=47 K, beta=1.6, for L_FIR

evidence.quote: we follow the literature and assume a dust temperature of 47 K and a dust emissivity index of $\beta=1.6$

continuum subtraction method and line-free channels

method.value: CASA reduction, natural weighting; total flux in 0.75" radius aperture; Gaussian line fit for redshift and flux

evidence.quote: We measured the total flux of the quasar host galaxy in an aperture with a radius of 0.75$''$.

assumptions.value: L_FIR from dust SED with T=47 K, beta=1.6, 42.5-122.5 um

evidence.quote: Far-infrared luminosities, $L_{\mathrm{FIR}}$, are computed by integrating the dust spectral energy distribution (SED) between the rest-frame wavelengths 42.5 and 122.5 $\mu$m

method.value: Four 3D models (Disk A, B, C, Rot+Jet D) convolved with the primary beam, fit to cube with chi-squared on bootstrapped pixels

evidence.quote: we do not sum up all of the pixels in our data, but instead use a bootstrap method, whereby we randomly select $N$ pixels from the data cube and calculate the $\chi^2$ value of these pixels.

key_parameters.value: Model velocities -216 to +216 km/s, excluding channels affected by close companion

evidence.quote: The model cube has velocities that range from –216 to +216 km s$^{-1}$.

fitting.value: emcee affine-invariant MCMC, flat priors, initial guesses from visual inspection

evidence.quote: For all parameters, we assume flat priors, and we initiate the parameters with rough estimates from visual inspection of the data.

validation.value: Verified initial guesses do not affect MCMC results

evidence.quote: We have verified that these initial guesses do not affect the results of the MCMC analysis.

method.value: Chevalier (1974) expanding shell energy formula with d~0.5 kpc, n=1e5 cm^-3, v_exp~80 km/s; compare with SNe and AGN energy

evidence.quote: Taken together, we derive a required energy of $\sim$$3\times10^{59}$ erg

assumptions.value: 5% of accreted energy deposited as thermal energy in ISM; 1 SN per 200 Msun of stars

evidence.quote: Assuming that 5% of the accreted energy is deposited as thermal energy in the ISM (cite: dim05)

method.value: Gaussian fits to [C II] of companions; SFR from De Looze relation; H2 mass with alpha_[CII]=31

evidence.quote: Molecular gas mass, derived from the \[C II\] luminosity using a $L_\mathrm{[CII]}$-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $\alpha_\mathrm{[CII]} = 31$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$/$L_\ensuremath{\odot}$
The data were reduced using the Common Astronomy Software Application package (cite: mul07)

used_for.value: MCMC sampling of kinematic model parameters

evidence.quote: we have used the affine invariant MCMC ensemble sampler code, `emcee` (cite: for13)
The total continuum flux density is 5.34$\pm$0.19 mJy around the \[C II\] line
The total brightness of the \[C II\] line is 5.43$\pm$0.33 Jy km s$^{-1}$
$L_\mathrm{[CII]}$ = $(5.90\pm0.36)\times10^9$ $L_\ensuremath{\odot}$
we derive a required energy of $\sim$$3\times10^{59}$ erg

findings_qualitative.value: Gas is dispersion-dominated with little ordered rotation, not settled in a disk; two ~0.5 kpc [C II] cavities offset from the black hole; three [C II] companions.

evidence.quote: The gas has a high velocity dispersion with little ordered motion along the line of sight

claims.hypothesis: Gas kinematics are consistent with a simple rotating disk
claims.experiment: Fit four 3D models to the [C II] cube with MCMC
claims.result: Constant-velocity disk inconsistent; truncated disk and others do not give adequate fits
claims.finding: Gas is dispersion-dominated and not yet settled in a disk

evidence.quote: the kinematics are inconsistent with a simple rotating disk with a constant velocity (Disk A)

claims.hypothesis: Cavities are produced by supernovae or by AGN energy
claims.experiment: Compute required energy and compare with SN and AGN output
claims.result: ~3e59 erg, equal to 300 million SNe, AGN needs ~2.5 Myr
claims.finding: Energy must originate from the AGN, without suppressing star formation

evidence.quote: the required energy to create the cavities would be generated in only 2.5 million years

claims.experiment: Search the deep cube for [C II] emitters
claims.result: Three [C II] emitters at the quasar redshift
claims.finding: Interactions may have triggered star formation and AGN activity

evidence.quote: Our new data reveal the presence of three \[C II\] emitters at the same redshift as the quasar

why_this_data.value: Resolve the host structure and explore its kinematics, and probe black hole sphere of influence scales

evidence.quote: To resolve the structure of the host galaxy and explore its detailed kinematics, we observed J0305–3150

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Supernova-driven cavities rejected as they would need ~40 Myr of constant SFR in a restricted volume

evidence.quote: would then require a constant star formation rate over $\sim$40 million years in a very restricted volume

limitations_admitted.value: Models are oversimplified, assuming a smooth decreasing intensity profile

evidence.quote: This clearly is an oversimplification, as the moment 0 map shows obvious evidence of nonexponential emission

referee_caveats_inferred: Simple parametric models do not fit; conclusions about cavity origin are qualitative
Energy estimate relies on assumed density from another paper and an adopted v_exp
Uncertainties on L_FIR ignore SED shape (factor 2-3)

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project code given in acknowledgments; public status not stated
